title: Gas Station
pattern: Greedy: restart after the tank runs dry
statement: Gas stations stand on a circular route. Station `i` gives you `gas[i]`, and driving from station `i` to the next one costs `cost[i]`. Starting with an empty tank, return the index of the station from which you can drive once around the circle, or `-1` if that is impossible. (If an answer exists it is unique.)

example.why: From station 4 the tank goes 3, 4, 1, 2, 0 — it never drops below zero.

idea: If the total gas is less than the total cost, no start can work. If it is at least the total cost, some start **always** works.

Try a start and keep the tank level. If the tank goes negative at station `i`, this start fails — and so does **every station between the start and i**: each of them would arrive at `i` with even less gas (we reached them with a non-negative tank).
So skip them all: the next candidate is station `i + 1`, with an empty tank. The last candidate left after one pass is the answer (if the totals allow one).

steps.text: Our example: **`gas = [5,1,2,3,4], cost = [4,4,1,5,1]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.

steps.text: `current_gas` is the tank on a trip starting at `start_station` (first candidate: station 0). `total_gas` adds up gas − cost over the whole circle to see whether a trip is possible at all.

steps.text: Station 0: fill up 5, then burn 4 driving on. Net +1 → tank = **1** (overall balance 1).

steps.text: Station 1: fill up 1, then burn 4 driving on. Net -3 → tank = **-2** (overall balance -2).

steps.text: The tank went **negative** after station 1, so the trip from station 0 fails. Starting later, at station 1, cannot help either: that trip would reach this point with even less gas. Skip ahead — next candidate: station **2**, with an empty tank.

steps.text: Station 2: fill up 2, then burn 1 driving on. Net +1 → tank = **1** (overall balance -1).

views.title: gas − cost  (what each station adds to the tank)

steps.text: Station 3: fill up 3, then burn 5 driving on. Net -2 → tank = **-1** (overall balance -3).

views.title: gas − cost  (what each station adds to the tank)

steps.text: The tank went **negative** after station 3, so the trip from station 2 fails. Starting later, at station 3, cannot help either: that trip would reach this point with even less gas. Skip ahead — next candidate: station **4**, with an empty tank.

views.title: gas − cost  (what each station adds to the tank)

steps.text: Station 4: fill up 4, then burn 1 driving on. Net +3 → tank = **3** (overall balance 0).

views.title: gas − cost  (what each station adds to the tank)

steps.text: The overall balance is 0 ≥ 0, so a full circle is possible — and station **4** is the only candidate that survived.

views.title: gas − cost  (what each station adds to the tank)

steps.text: Done — the answer is **`4`**. From station 4 the tank goes 3, 4, 1, 2, 0 — it never drops below zero.
